rationale: Neither candidate hits the two actual ground-truth concerns (aligning the latency timeline split with PR #5857's format, and whether FL2VA/Ref2VA were both actually tested) — both reviews focus entirely on independently-discovered code-grounded issues instead, so recall is low and roughly tied. Both are deeply verified against the codebase with specific file:line citations and agree on several real defects (timeout default 600s not 1800s, the 49-vs-50 per-step denominator, missing --enable-diffusion-pipeline-profiler flag, 128GB decimal/binary conflation, missing README entry), giving both high precision. Y edges ahead on actionability and coverage: it catches a genuinely valuable functional bug (short_edge must be 768, contradicting the recipe's 'keep short edge at 576' Ref2VA guidance) that X misses entirely, presents findings in a clearer human-readable structure with an explicit verdict, and adds useful process gaps (missing environment/version provenance, no prerequisites section).
